decision: defined done as a measured drop in clicks and typed fields on core journeys, each journey still reaching a checked end state on the real app
why: brainless to use is an opinion until it is counted, so every journey gets a before and after number

decision: started local Postgres and proved the existing stack harness boots the whole app here
why: critics and the scorecard both need the real app, not a reading of the code

decision: all journey interactions go through one counted ui helper, and run-all refuses journey files that click or type outside it
why: a hand-reported step count can be gamed, a counter in the path of every click cannot

decision: will not file GitHub issues for the proposals (ux-flow phase 4)
why: issues are posted in the owner's name and were not asked for, and the top proposals get built in this run anyway

decision: mapped the app from source, then sent ten story writers out, one per topic, with a consolidator after them
why: ux-flow needs a story catalog with ideal step counts and alternate routes before it can critique anything

decision: added subtext reduction to scope: every helper line gets a cut, shorten or keep verdict
why: the owner asked mid-run to reduce subtext too

decision: wrote the sign-in journey by hand and ran it on the served app
why: wanted the counting helper proven on one real journey before nine critics build on it

decision: picked ten journeys by how often a clinic runs them and gave each critic its own patient on one shared seeded app
why: one running app is cheaper than ten, and separate patients stop critics breaking each other's data
result: 7 critics running, 3 wait for their story files

decision: critics run on the cheaper tier and write proposals only, I judge and rank them
why: critics do the walking and counting, the accept or reject call stays with one judge

decision: story catalog finished: 77 stories, 71 percent of features covered, the Reports topic produced no file
why: the catalog is what ux-flow reads; the Reports gap is covered by the j07 critic walking the report screens live

decision: rewrote the seed's record ids to the shape the app's own validators accept, and gave every seeded appointment a token
why: two critics hit errors that came from my demo data and not from the app: payments rejected the id shape, and one appointment without a token made every booking for today fail
result: j01 j02 j05 j09 pass on a fresh stack with the fixed seed

decision: restarted the shared app with the fixed seed and told the seven critics still working
why: findings made on broken demo data would be false, so they re-check anything that looked like an id or booking error

decision: tightened the walk-in journey so it fails unless the patient lands on today's list
why: its critic had loosened the goal to pass while bookings for today were failing
result: edited, replayed in the baseline run

decision: each journey now starts from a fresh seed inside one run
why: the first full run failed two journeys only because earlier journeys had billed and prescribed on the same data

decision: sign-in in the harness waits and retries when the app rate-limits logins
why: ten journeys back to back hit the login limit, a person signing in once a day does not
result: all ten pass in one run

decision: recorded the baseline on unchanged app code: 113 actions across ten journeys
why: every later claim of simpler is measured against this file
result: 10 of 10 PASS; frontend jest 149 suites 1581 tests pass

decision: rejected one-click booking with no dialog, one-tap payment buttons per mode, and silently applying a remembered dose
why: each saves a click by removing the only pause before a booking, a payment or a prescription line is recorded, and a slip there costs more than the click

decision: the calendar legend gets collapsed behind a closed control, not deleted
why: an owner product rule says the legend must name both calendars and explain Confirm, so the content stays and only its place changes

decision: split the build into six units by screen family, each in its own work copy
why: the units touch different files, so they can run side by side without stepping on each other
